role: Software Engineer Intern (First Play)  - Summer 2027 (Mountain View, CA)
jd:
LinkedIn is the world’s largest professional network, built to create economic opportunity for every member of the global workforce. Our products help people make powerful connections, discover exciting opportunities, build necessary skills, and gain valuable insights every day. We’re also committed to providing transformational opportunities for our own employees by investing in their growth. We aspire to create a culture that’s built on trust, care, inclusion, and fun – where everyone can succeed.  


Join us to transform the way the world works.  



Job Description


This internship role will be based in Mountain View, California. 


At LinkedIn, our approach to flexible work is centered on trust and optimized for culture, connection, clarity, and the evolving needs of our business. The work location of this role is hybrid, meaning it will be performed both from home and from a LinkedIn office on select days, as determined by the business needs of the team. 


First Play is LinkedIn’s software engineering internship designed for students earlier in their computer science journey to build strong engineering foundations through real-world experience. Interns contribute to meaningful, scoped engineering projects, tackle real technical challenges, and gain firsthand experience building software at LinkedIn.


As software development continues to evolve, First Play gives interns the opportunity to grow as engineers in an AI-native engineering environment. Interns will gain hands-on experience with modern engineering practices, use AI-powered development tools, and explore how AI and emerging technologies are shaping the way software is built. Through mentorship, collaboration, and ongoing feedback, interns will strengthen their technical skills, learn from engineers across LinkedIn, and build the foundation to take on increasingly complex engineering challenges.


Candidates must be currently enrolled in an undergraduate degree program, with an expected graduation date of December 2028 or later.


The First Play internship is a 12-week program with two available sessions:



- May 24, 2027 – August 13, 2027
- June 14, 2027 – September 3, 2027


Responsibilities



- Contribute to meaningful, scoped software engineering projects and apply programming and problem-solving skills to real-world technical challenges. 
- Write, test, debug, and iterate on code while developing familiarity with engineering practices such as version control, code reviews, and continuous integration. 
- Use AI-powered development tools and emerging technologies as part of the software development process while continuing to build strong engineering fundamentals. 
- Work with engineers to solve technical problems, incorporate feedback, and strengthen software engineering skills. 
- Participate in First Play cohort experiences and LinkedIn’s broader intern programming to build connections, develop skills, and engage with the LinkedIn community. 

Qualifications


Basic Qualifications



- Pursuing a B.A. or B.S. degree in Computer Science or a related technical field. 
- Programming experience in Python, Java, C, C++, C#, Rust, or a similar object-oriented programming language. 


Preferred Qualifications



- Understanding of foundational data structures, algorithms, and object-oriented programming concepts. 
- Experience applying programming concepts through coursework, class projects, hackathons, personal coding projects, or other technical work. 
- Experience building, testing, debugging, or iterating on code through coursework, projects, hackathons, or other technical work. 
- Experience breaking down technical problems and developing solutions through coursework, projects, or other technical experiences. 


Suggested Skills



- Programming Foundations
- Data Structures and Algorithms
- Technical Problem-Solving


As part of the application process for this role, after an initial qualifications review, candidates are required to successfully complete the HackerRank online code challenge. Instructions for completion of the code challenge will be sent to you if your application is selected to move forward in the process. 


LinkedIn is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices.  

  

The pay range for this role is $45 to $55. Actual compensation packages are based on several factors that are unique to each candidate, including but not limited to skill set, depth of experience, certifications, and specific work location. This may be different in other locations due to differences in the cost of labor.  

  

The total compensation package for this position may also include annual performance bonus, stock, benefits and/or other applicable incentive compensation plans. For more information, visit https://careers.linkedin.com/benefits. 



Additional Information

We seek candidates with a wide range of perspectives and backgrounds and we are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. LinkedIn considers qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, creed, gender, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, marital status, pregnancy, sex, gender expression or identity, sexual orientation, citizenship, or any other legally protected class.

Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all. 

Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever.

### Department Overview

The Digital Solutions and Enterprise Applications team develops innovative software platforms that enable business operations, automation, and digital transformation across Micron. By using modern software engineering practices, AI technologies, and cloud-native solutions, the team delivers scalable applications that improve productivity, decision-making, and operational efficiency throughout the organization.

### Position Overview

As a Software Engineering Intern, you will help design, develop, and support software solutions that address critical business needs across Micron. You will gain hands-on experience building full-stack applications, AI agents, automation solutions, and enterprise platforms while working with modern development tools, cloud technologies, and AI-enabled engineering practices.

### Responsibilities

 * Design, develop, and enhance software solutions that improve business processes, productivity, and operational efficiency.
 * Build and integrate AI agents, intelligent automation solutions, and Model Context Protocol (MCP)-enabled applications that support business workflows and decision-making.
 * Develop full-stack applications using modern programming languages, databases, APIs, and web technologies.
 * Create monitoring, reporting, and analytics capabilities that provide operational visibility, usage insights, and system health metrics.
 * Collaborate with cross-functional teams to implement scalable, secure, and reliable software solutions while supporting continuous improvement initiatives and AI-enabled development workflows.

### Minimum Qualifications

 * 0-2 years of relevant experience through internships, academic projects, research, software development activities, hackathons, or technical work experience.
 * Currently pursuing or recently completed a Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, Information Technology, or a related technical field.
 * Experience with one or more programming languages such as Python, C#, Java, C/C++, JavaScript, or similar technologies.
 * Understanding of software development fundamentals, object-oriented programming, software architecture, and application design principles.
 * Familiarity with web technologies, databases, APIs, version control systems, and modern development environments.
 * Demonstrated experience using AI-enabled tools and large language models (LLMs) such as GitHub Copilot, Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, or similar technologies to improve software development productivity and problem-solving.
 * Strong analytical, problem-solving, organizational, written, and verbal communication skills.
 * Ability to work effectively in a collaborative team environment.

### Preferred Qualifications

 * Experience developing AI agents, AI-assisted workflows, prompt engineering solutions, or generative AI applications.
 * Familiarity with Model Context Protocol (MCP), agentic workflows, tool integration frameworks, or AI orchestration platforms.
 * Experience with frontend technologies such as JavaScript, Angular, AJAX, CSS, or similar web development frameworks.
 * Knowledge of databases including Microsoft SQL Server, MySQL, MongoDB, or comparable platforms.
 * Familiarity with Linux environments, containerization technologies such as Docker or Kubernetes, and cloud-native development practices.
 * Experience with web servers and application platforms such as Apache, Tomcat, IIS, Node.js, or similar technologies.
 * Experience using GitHub, CI/CD pipelines, automated testing, or software delivery workflows.
 * Demonstrated interest in applying AI, automation, and emerging technologies to solve business challenges and improve enterprise productivity.
 * Strong leadership, communication, and collaboration skills with the ability to work across technical and business teams.

role: Graduate Intern – Power Data Analysis for AI Data Centers
jd:
Posting Title 
Graduate Intern – Power Data Analysis for AI Data Centers . 
 Location 
CO - Golden . 
 Position Type 
Intern (Fixed Term) . 
 Hours Per Week 
40 . 
 Working at NLR 
NLR is located at the foothills of the Rocky Mountains in Golden, Colorado is the nation's primary laboratory for energy systems research and development. 
 Join the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR), where world-class scientists, engineers, and experts are accelerating energy innovation through breakthrough research and systems integration. From our mission to our collaborative culture, NLR stands out in the research community for its commitment to an affordable and secure energy future. Spanning foundational science to applied systems engineering and analysis, we focus on solving complex challenges to deliver advanced, secure, reliable, and cost-effective energy solutions. Our work helps strengthen U.S. industries, support job creation, and promote national economic growth.
 
 At NLR, you'll find a mission-driven environment supported by state-of-the-art facilities, multidisciplinary research teams, and strong collaborations with industry, academia, and other national laboratories. We offer robust professional development opportunities, and a competitive benefits package designed to support your career and well-being.

 Job Description 
 The Digital Twins and Scalable Workflows group in NLR’s Computational Science Center has an opening for a graduate student researcher in data center power analytics, with an emphasis on the electrical behavior of AI workloads. AI is driving rapid growth in data center electricity demand, and the sub-second power swings of GPU workloads are a growing concern for grid stability. This project measures the electrical power of GPU racks on NLR’s Kestrel supercomputer while AI training, inference, and agentic workloads run, and uses those measurements to build models that predict realistic power behavior for workloads that haven’t been measured.

 The researcher will be the project’s eyes on the data: reviewing the power measurements from every experiment, identifying anomalies and tracing their causes through system telemetry and profiling data, and labeling power ramps and other critical events. The researcher will also build an automated event detector, trained and evaluated on their own labeled data, that flags ramps and anomalies in new measurements.
 We are looking for a curious, detail-oriented researcher with strong data analysis skills and an interest in energy, computing, and the grid. The successful candidate will work closely with NLR researchers in high-performance computing, power systems, and data center operations, and will have the opportunity to present and publish their work.
 Responsibilities include:
 
• Review power measurements from AI workload experiments for anomalies and data quality issues, using an interactive visualization workbench. 
• Hand-label power ramps, load steps, and other critical events, and identify regions that exemplify characteristic workload behavior, following a documented labeling protocol. 
• Investigate unexplained behavior by correlating power measurements with GPU telemetry, profiling data, job logs, and system configuration, and document the findings. 
• Design, build, and evaluate an automated detector for power ramps and anomalies, trained and tested on labeled data. 
• Present results and contribute to technical reports, papers, and conference presentations. . 
 Basic Qualifications 
Minimum of a 3.0 cumulative grade point average.

Undergraduate: Must be enrolled as a full-time student in a bachelor’s degree program from an accredited institution. 
Post Undergraduate: Earned a bachelor’s degree within the past 12 months. Eligible for an internship period of up to one year.

Graduate: Must be enrolled as a full-time student in a master’s degree program from an accredited institution. 
Post Graduate: Earned a master’s degree within the past 12 months. Eligible for an internship period of up to one year.
Graduate + PhD: Completed master’s degree and enrolled as PhD student from an accredited institution. 

Please Note:
• Applicants are responsible for uploading official or unofficial school transcripts, as part of the application process.
• If selected for position, a letter of recommendation will be required as part of the hiring process.
• Must meet educational requirements prior to employment start date. 
 * Must meet educational requirements prior to employment start date. 
 
 Additional Required Qualifications 

 Preferred Qualifications 
 
• Careful attention to detail, and the ability to follow and help refine a structured review process. 
• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including clear documentation of findings. 
• Ability to work independently and to raise questions early. 
• Experience analyzing time-series or signal data (for example, spectral analysis or event detection). 
• Familiarity with GPU computing, AI/ML workloads, or HPC systems (for example, Slurm). 
• Programming experience in Python for data analysis. 
• Experience with machine learning for classification or detection. 
• Background in power systems or electrical measurements. 
• Experience with data labeling, annotation, or data quality review. 
 . 
 Job Application Submission Window 
 The anticipated closing window for application submission is up to 30 days and may be extended as needed.

 Annual Salary Range (based on full-time 40 hours per week) 
Job Profile: / Annual Salary Range: $44,500 - $71,200 

 NLR takes into consideration a candidate’s education, training, and experience, expected quality and quantity of work, required travel (if any), external market and internal value, including seniority and merit systems, and internal pay alignment when determining the salary level for potential new employees. In compliance with the Colorado Equal Pay for Equal Work Act, a potential new employee’s salary history will not be used in compensation decisions.

 Benefits Summary 
Benefits include medical, dental, and vision insurance; 403(b) Employee Savings Plan with employer match*; and sick leave (where required by law). NLR employees may be eligible for, but are not guaranteed, performance-, merit-, and achievement- based awards that include a monetary component. Some positions may be eligible for relocation expense reimbursement. Internships projected to be less than 20 hours per week are not eligible for medical, dental, or vision benefits. 
 * Based on eligibility rules

 Badging Requirement 
NLR is subject to Department of Energy (DOE) access restrictions. All employees must also be able to obtain and maintain a federal Personal Identity Verification (PIV) card as required by Homeland Security Presidential Directive 12 (HSPD-12), which includes a favorable background investigation. Intern assignments extending beyond six months will be subject to this requirement. 
 Drug Free Workplace 
 NLR is committed to maintaining a drug-free workplace in accordance with the federal Drug-Free Workplace Act and complies with federal laws prohibiting the possession and use of illegal drugs. Under federal law, marijuana remains an illegal drug.
 
 If you are offered employment at NLR, you must pass a pre-employment drug test prior to commencing employment. Unless prohibited by state or local law, the pre-employment drug test will include marijuana. If you test positive on the pre-employment drug test, your offer of employment may be withdrawn.

 Submission Guidelines 
 Please note that in order to be considered an applicant for any position at NLR you must submit an application form for each position for which you believe you are qualified. Applications are not kept on file for future positions. Please include a cover letter and resume with each position application.
 
 . 
 Equal Opportunity Employer 
 All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard basis of age (40 and over), color, disability, gender identity, genetic information, marital status, domestic partner status, military or veteran status, national origin/ancestry, race, religion, creed, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding), sexual orientation, and any other applicable status protected by federal, state, or local laws.
